kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the four printed tables — 4 patterns (the metoclopramide tardive-dyskinesia timeline, the isoniazid triple-neuro-toxin presentation, the visual-disturbance color-match, the metronidazole disulfiram-like reaction), 4 traps (the twin movement rows, INH's three faces, the digoxin-yellow/PDE-5-blue/ethambutol-color visual coding, the mesna-preventable hemorrhagic cystitis vs the cisplatin renal rows), 3 pivots, 8 recall cards — plus the organ-system routing pivot that ties all four tables together.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the four tables' facts only; the attack structure, the distractor designs, and the timeline-based discrimination training are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The four-move reading protocol (NAME THE SIGN → NAME THE PATHWAY → NAME THE ROW → NAME THE DRUG, then check its other appearances) and the route-every-reaction-to-the-pathway-it-disrupts framing of the whole page.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints four parallel tables and never asks the learner to route a clinical sign through pathway → row → drug; the protocol and the pathway-first framing are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + blocks[6] the steps block + the registry visual's four-move protocol band

kypExtensions.summary: The twin-rows synthesis: the observation that Parkinson-like syndrome and tardive dyskinesia print IDENTICAL causal agents (antipsychotics, metoclopramide) and are separated only by the direction of receptor adaptation — acute D2 blockade (down-state, cogwheel rigidity of arm) vs chronic blockade with compensatory D2 up-regulation (overshoot, choreiform movements, the empty printed NOTES cell) — built out as mechanism 1 (dopamine-pathway-map), the compare block, and the visual's Zone A fork.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the two rows adjacently with the same agents and a one-sign note; the receptor-adaptation fork, the down-state/overshoot framing, and the RIGID EARLY, WRITHING LATE rule are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: mechanisms[0] + blocks[5] the compare block + usmle.patterns[0]/traps[0]/miniCase + the visual's Zone A

kypExtensions.summary: The cross-table repeater map: isoniazid ×3 (peripheral neuropathy, seizures, optic neuritis), cisplatin ×3 (peripheral neuropathy, Fanconi syndrome, nephrotoxicity), antipsychotics ×3 (both movement rows + antimuscarinic), metoclopramide ×2, ifosfamide ×2, tetracyclines ×2, cephalosporins ×2 — with the pyridoxine (B6) thread tying INH's neuropathy to its seizure risk.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source never points out which drugs appear on multiple rows or across multiple tables; the double-dipper inventory and the INH-triple-neuro-toxin hook are KYP's cross-referencing synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: core.why + blocks[7] the exam callout + mnemonics[1-2] + the visual's Zone C chips

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP mnemonics (RIGID EARLY, WRITHING LATE · INH, THE TRIPLE NEURO TOXIN · THE DOUBLE-DIPPERS · RECEPTOR BLOCK, ENZYME BLOCK). First Aid's own seven red in-cell mnemonic lines (“Cis, it’s very painful peripherally” · “Crime and debt Always grow head tension” · “With seizures, I bit my tongue” · “These horrible drugs iirritate Precious eyes” · “Remember the 5 P’s” + the in-cell P's of Pee/Pain-free/Penicillins/PPIs/rifamPin · “My nose cannot breathe bad air” · “Sorry pals, can’t go mingle”) are carried ATTRIBUTED inside the verbatim tables and are NOT counted among the four KYP codes.
kypExtensions.rationale: The seven mnemonic lines are the source's own red print (VLM + raw-span census, staging-ph25/vlm-census.txt); the four ALL-CAPS structural hooks are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: mnemonics + blocks[8] the memory callout + the visual's mnemonic renderings

notes: FULL page: pdf 272 / book 250 carries FOUR three-column tables (all DRUG REACTION / CAUSAL AGENTS / NOTES) under the banner PHARMACOLOGY—TOXICITIES AND ADVERSE EFFECTS, all owned by this topic: [1] Drug reactions—neurologic (7 rows, printed order: Cinchonism → Parkinson-like syndrome → Peripheral neuropathy → Idiopathic intracranial hypertension → Seizures → Tardive dyskinesia → Visual disturbances), [2] Drug reactions—renal/genitourinary (4 rows: Fanconi syndrome → Hemorrhagic cystitis → Interstitial nephritis → Nephrotoxicity), [3] Drug reactions—respiratory (2 rows: Dry cough → Pulmonary fibrosis), [4] Drug reactions—multiorgan (2 rows: Antimuscarinic → Disulfiram-like reaction) — all carried VERBATIM in the note's four table blocks in PRINTED row order. CENSUS (pdfimages): ZERO raster images — pure vector/text; no margin notes, figures, or icons (VLM-confirmed). VLM WAS AVAILABLE this session: ONE 120dpi glm-4.6v pass (staging-ph25/vlm-census.txt) confirmed the four tables' row order, the empty NOTES cells (tardive dyskinesia, Fanconi syndrome, nephrotoxicity, dry cough, antimuscarinic), the disulfiram-row ownership of “Sorry pals, can’t go mingle”, and the red/teal color furniture; a second VLM pass was not needed — the two disputes the 120dpi read left were adjudicated deterministically with PyMuPDF raw spans + pdftotext -bbox (documented in vlm-census.txt): (1) the visual-disturbances mnemonic PRINTS the source's own double-i “iirritate” (a red-bold 'ii' glyph pair — i = Isoniazid, i = Ivabradine — before black 'rritate'; the VLM smoothed to single-i; carried verbatim); (2) the apostrophes in it’s/5 P’s/can’t print as U+2019 (the VLM claimed straight quotes). Also raw-span confirmed: the in-cell 5-P mnemonic with the red capital P printed INSIDE “rifamPin” (plus Pee/Pain-free/Penicillins/PPIs and a red “s” on sulfa); the pulmonary-fibrosis cell ending exactly “bleomycin, busulfan, amiodarone”; “H1-blockers” printing with a subscript 1 (cache merges); “growth hormones” printing plural; drug-reaction names in teal, mnemonic initials in red. TEXT-LAYER INTERLEAVE QUIRKS (documented in census + note captions): the respiratory NOTES header extracts AFTER both data rows (cache lines 103-110 → 112 → 114); the multiorgan footer slug extracts BETWEEN the disulfiram causal agents and the NOTES header + mnemonic + timestamp (cache lines 129 → 131 → 133/135/137); the 'SEC TION II' header-space artifact. DrugCards were FOLDED into the verbatim tables + the compare/steps blocks rather than authored as a drugs[] array — the DrugCard shape (one drug with mechanism/uses/adverse cells) does not fit a reaction→causal-agents table; the decision is documented in the note's header comment. Related-topic ids: the three parallel batch-sibling ids (drug-reactions-hematologic, drug-reactions-endocrine, toxicity-treatments) are being produced by the sibling tasks of batch ph21-ph25 and are registered by the promotion step; stroke-syndromes is a verified existing note id. Quirks vs the batch spec: the spec's content map mentioned a 'headache' row and a 'cognition' row for the neuro table — the page prints NO such rows (cognition appears only inside the cinchonism NOTES cell, 'cognitive impairment'); 'whatever rows print' governs, and the seven printed rows are carried. The note is 733 lines and the visual 261 (viewBox 0 0 1102 1344), within the brief's 600-750 / 250-400 budgets. Outputs are STAGED under .usmle-pipeline-cache/staging-ph25/ — nothing is written into content/ (chapters, content manifests, notes/index.ts, and the visual registry are owned by the promotion step; the note's visualId 'drug-reaction-neurologic-map' is therefore not yet in visuals/registry.tsx by design).
